"""Web-search provider adapters for the Monitor search surface (#1134).

Currently a single provider — Serper (google.serper.dev). The adapter is a

)

"""GDELT DOC 2.0 news-search adapter (#1138).

A thin, pure adapter over the GDELT Project's keyless DOC 2.0 API. It mirrors
:mod:`monitor_svc.search.serper` — same stub gate, same typed error surface —
with two GDELT-specific wrinkles:

- **Keyless.** GDELT needs no API key, so — unlike Serper — there is no
  :class:`ProviderKeyReader` parameter and the reader is never consulted for a
  news search. :func:`gdelt_available` is a constant ``True`` and makes NO
  network call: it sits on the hot ``GetSearchProviders`` path, where a live
  probe would waste GDELT's ~1 request / 5s budget (#1138 review).
- **ISO→FIPS country mapping.** GDELT's ``sourcecountry`` filter expects
  FIPS-10-4 codes, NOT the ISO-3166 alpha-2 codes the frontend sends (the
  classic gotcha: ISO ``CN`` = China but FIPS ``CH`` = China, while ISO ``CH`` =
  Switzerland maps to FIPS ``SZ``). :func:`iso_to_fips` translates; an unknown
  ISO code yields ``""`` so the caller omits ``sourcecountry`` (worldwide)
  rather than sending a bogus filter.

Mode precedence: ``MONITOR_SEARCH_STUB == "1"`` → deterministic canned rows (no
network); otherwise a live GET to the DOC 2.0 endpoint.

Filter → DOC 2.0 param mapping (see :func:`search_news`): ``mode=ArtList``,
``format=json``, ``maxrecords`` (count clamped 1..250, default 50), ``timespan``
(DAY→``1d`` / WEEK→``1w`` / MONTH→``1m`` / YEAR→``1y``; ANY/UNSPEC omit),
``sourcecountry`` (ISO→FIPS), ``sort=DateDesc``. A ``domain`` filter is folded
into the query as GDELT's ``domain:<d>`` operator.

Error mapping (live): HTTP 429 → :class:`SearchThrottled` carrying the upstream
``Retry-After`` seconds (default 60 when absent/unparseable); any other non-2xx,
transport error, timeout, or non-JSON 2xx body → :class:`SearchUnavailable`. The
gRPC handler turns these into ``RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`` (with a
``google.rpc.RetryInfo`` detail) / ``UNAVAILABLE``.

The adapter reads the ``search_pb2`` filter enums (SearchTimeRange /
NewsResultType) only to map them onto DOC 2.0 params; it returns plain
:class:`NewsResultData` values the handler maps back onto ``search_pb2`` and
never touches gRPC.
"""

_DOC_URL = "https://api.gdeltproject.org/api/v2/doc/doc"
_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_S = 10.0

#: GDELT's ``maxrecords`` bounds. DOC 2.0 caps at 250; we default to 50 when the
#: caller passes a non-positive count, and clamp anything above the ceiling.
_DEFAULT_MAXRECORDS = 50
_MIN_MAXRECORDS = 1
_MAX_MAXRECORDS = 250

#: Default coverage window when the caller passes a blank timespan.
_DEFAULT_TIMESPAN = "1d"
#: Broad standing query for the Home coverage volume (best-effort; the honest
#: acceptance path is the stub's fixed count).
_COVERAGE_QUERY = "news"
#: Fixed stub coverage volume for the Home CoverageStrip GDELT chip.
_STUB_COVERAGE_COUNT = 42

#: How long a live coverage count is served from the server-side cache before a
#: refresh is attempted (5 minutes). The Home chip loads on every dashboard hit,
#: but GDELT allows only ~1 request / 5s per IP — a per-load live call gets 429'd
#: (blank chip) AND steals the rate-limit budget from real user searches. Serving
#: a slightly-aged cached number keeps the chip populated without hammering GDELT.
_COVERAGE_TTL_S = 300.0
#: Short cache window applied after a FAILED refresh, so an outage doesn't trigger
#: a fresh upstream call on every single load (we serve the last good value, or 0).
_COVERAGE_ERROR_BACKOFF_S = 30.0

#: Server-side TTL cache for :func:`news_coverage`, keyed by RESOLVED timespan so
#: distinct windows don't clobber one another. Value is ``(count, expires_at)``
#: where ``expires_at`` is a :func:`time.monotonic` deadline.
_coverage_cache: dict[str, tuple[int, float]] = {}
#: Serialises refreshes so concurrent callers don't stampede GDELT — one fetches,
#: the rest re-check the cache under the lock and reuse the fresh value. Recreated
#: by :func:`_reset_coverage_cache` so a test's fresh event loop never inherits a
#: lock bound to a closed loop.
_coverage_lock: asyncio.Lock = asyncio.Lock()


def _reset_coverage_cache() -> None:
    """Clear the coverage TTL cache and its lock (test hook).

    Drops every cached ``(count, expires_at)`` entry and rebinds the stampede
    lock so module state never leaks between tests (or across event loops).
    """
    global _coverage_lock  # module-state reset hook: rebind the stampede lock
    _coverage_cache.clear()
    _coverage_lock = asyncio.Lock()


#: Retry-After fallback (seconds) when GDELT 429s without a parseable header.
_DEFAULT_RETRY_AFTER = 60

# SearchTimeRange enum -> GDELT ``timespan``. ANY / UNSPECIFIED omit ``timespan``
# (GDELT then uses its own default recency window). Keyed by ``int`` so a plain
# ``time_range: int`` lookup type-checks.

class SearchError(Exception):
    """Base class for GDELT news-search adapter failures."""


class SearchUnavailable(SearchError):
    """The provider failed/refused the request (non-2xx, transport, non-JSON)."""


class SearchThrottled(SearchError):
    """GDELT rate-limited the request (HTTP 429).

    Carries :attr:`retry_after` — the upstream ``Retry-After`` seconds (or the
    :data:`_DEFAULT_RETRY_AFTER` fallback) — which the handler propagates as a
    ``google.rpc.RetryInfo`` detail on the ``RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`` status.
    """

    def __init__(self, message: str = "", *, retry_after: int = _DEFAULT_RETRY_AFTER) -> None:
        super().__init__(message)
        self.retry_after = retry_after


@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class NewsResultData:
    """One GDELT news article, provider-agnostic.

    ``source_domain`` is the article's publisher host with any leading ``www.``
    stripped. ``snippet`` is ALWAYS empty — GDELT's ArtList carries no
    per-article excerpt, so the card degrades to title + source + date.
    ``seen_date`` is the article date parsed from GDELT ``seendate`` into RFC3339
    UTC. ``thumbnail_url`` is set only for IMAGES-type results (the article's
    ``socialimage``); every other result class leaves it empty.
    """

    title: str
    url: str
    snippet: str = ""
    source_domain: str = ""
    source_country: str = ""
    seen_date: str = ""
    thumbnail_url: str = ""


def iso_to_fips(country_code: str) -> str:
    """Map an ISO-3166-1 alpha-2 code to its GDELT FIPS-10-4 code.

    Case-insensitive (the frontend sends lowercase). An empty or unknown code
    yields ``""`` so the caller omits ``sourcecountry`` entirely (worldwide)
    rather than sending a bogus filter GDELT would silently ignore.
    """
    return _ISO_TO_FIPS.get(country_code.strip().upper(), "")


def _stub_enabled() -> bool:
    """True when ``MONITOR_SEARCH_STUB`` is exactly ``"1"`` (shared with Serper)."""
    return os.environ.get("MONITOR_SEARCH_STUB") == "1"


def _source_domain(link: str, fallback: str = "") -> str:
    """Display domain: the URL host (or ``fallback``), minus a leading ``www.``."""
    host = urlparse(link).netloc or fallback
    prefix = "www."
    if host.startswith(prefix):
        return host[len(prefix) :]
    return host


def _parse_seendate(raw: str) -> str:
    """GDELT ``seendate`` (``YYYYMMDDTHHMMSSZ``) → RFC3339 UTC.

    Returns ``""`` on any unparseable value (the card then omits the date line)
    rather than raising.
    """
    try:
        dt = datetime.strptime(raw, "%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ").replace(tzinfo=UTC)
    except (ValueError, TypeError):
        return ""
    return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")


def _retry_after_seconds(response: httpx.Response) -> int:
    """Parse the ``Retry-After`` header (integer seconds), defaulting to
    :data:`_DEFAULT_RETRY_AFTER` when absent or non-integer."""
    raw = response.headers.get("Retry-After", "")
    try:
        seconds = int(raw)
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return _DEFAULT_RETRY_AFTER
    return seconds if seconds > 0 else _DEFAULT_RETRY_AFTER


# Deterministic canned news rows — distinct from Serper's web stub, each with a
# real RFC3339 seen_date so the date line + AC are exercised offline.
_STUB_NEWS_RESULTS: tuple[NewsResultData, ...] = (
    NewsResultData(
        title="Global summit concludes with joint communique",
        url="https://reuters.example.org/world/summit",
        source_domain="reuters.example.org",
        source_country="United Kingdom",
        seen_date="2026-01-03T09:15:00Z",
    ),
    NewsResultData(
        title="Regional election results certified",
        url="https://apnews.example.net/politics/election",
        source_domain="apnews.example.net",
        source_country="United States",
        seen_date="2026-01-02T18:40:00Z",
    ),
    NewsResultData(
        title="Markets rally on economic data",
        url="https://bbc.example.com/business/markets",
        source_domain="bbc.example.com",
        source_country="United Kingdom",
        seen_date="2026-01-01T12:00:00Z",
    ),
)


def _parse_articles(payload: dict[str, object], *, images_only: bool) -> list[NewsResultData]:
    """Map a DOC 2.0 ``articles[]`` array into :class:`NewsResultData`.

    Missing ``articles`` (or a non-list) yields ``[]``; non-dict entries are
    skipped. When ``images_only`` is set, only articles carrying a non-empty
    ``socialimage`` survive, and that image becomes their ``thumbnail_url``.
    """
    articles = payload.get("articles")
    if not isinstance(articles, list):
        return []
    results: list[NewsResultData] = []
    for item in articles:
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            continue
        social_image = str(item.get("socialimage", "") or "")
        if images_only and not social_image:
            continue
        url = str(item.get("url", ""))
        domain = str(item.get("domain", ""))
        results.append(
            NewsResultData(
                title=str(item.get("title", "")),
                url=url,
                snippet="",  # GDELT ArtList has no per-article excerpt.
                source_domain=_source_domain(url, fallback=domain),
                source_country=str(item.get("sourcecountry", "")),
                seen_date=_parse_seendate(str(item.get("seendate", ""))),
                thumbnail_url=social_image if images_only else "",
            )
        )
    return results


def _maxrecords(count: int) -> int:
    """Clamp ``count`` to GDELT's ``maxrecords`` bounds (1..250, default 50)."""
    if count <= 0:
        return _DEFAULT_MAXRECORDS
    return min(max(count, _MIN_MAXRECORDS), _MAX_MAXRECORDS)


async def search_news(
    query: str,
    count: int,
    *,
    country_code: str = "",
    time_range: int = search_pb2.SEARCH_TIME_RANGE_UNSPECIFIED,
    domain: str = "",
    result_type: int = search_pb2.NEWS_RESULT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED,
) -> list[NewsResultData]:
    """Run a GDELT news search for ``query`` returning up to ``count`` results.

    Mode precedence: stub → canned rows (no network); otherwise a live DOC 2.0
    GET. Filters map onto DOC 2.0 params (see the module docstring):
    ``country_code`` (ISO) → ``sourcecountry`` (FIPS; unknown omits it),
    ``time_range`` → ``timespan`` (ANY/UNSPEC omit), ``domain`` → a ``domain:``
    operator folded into the query, ``result_type`` IMAGES → keep only articles
    with a social image (set as ``thumbnail_url``). ``count`` is clamped to
    1..250 (default 50).

    Raises :class:`SearchThrottled` (429, carrying ``Retry-After``) or
    :class:`SearchUnavailable` (any other failure).
    """
    images_only = result_type == search_pb2.NEWS_RESULT_TYPE_IMAGES

    if _stub_enabled():
        rows = list(_STUB_NEWS_RESULTS)
        # Under stub the canned rows carry no social image, so IMAGES would
        # filter them all out; keep them so the offline/Cypress path still
        # renders. (The socialimage filter is exercised against a live payload.)
        return rows

    q = f"{query} domain:{domain.strip()}" if domain.strip() else query
    params: dict[str, str] = {
        "query": q,
        "mode": "ArtList",
        "format": "json",
        "maxrecords": str(_maxrecords(count)),
        "sort": "DateDesc",
    }
    timespan = _TIMESPAN_BY_TIME_RANGE.get(time_range)
    if timespan is not None:
        params["timespan"] = timespan
    fips = iso_to_fips(country_code)
    if fips:
        params["sourcecountry"] = fips

    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=httpx.Timeout(_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_S)) as client:
            resp = await client.get(_DOC_URL, params=params)
            resp.raise_for_status()
            # Decode inside the try: a 2xx with a non-JSON body (GDELT can answer
            # a bad query with an HTML/text error page) raises here and must
            # surface as the adapter's typed SearchUnavailable, not gRPC UNKNOWN.
            payload = resp.json()
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        if exc.response.status_code == 429:
            raise SearchThrottled(
                "gdelt rate limit exceeded",
                retry_after=_retry_after_seconds(exc.response),
            ) from exc
        raise SearchUnavailable(f"gdelt returned {exc.response.status_code}") from exc
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise SearchUnavailable(f"gdelt request failed: {exc}") from exc
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise SearchUnavailable("gdelt returned a non-JSON response") from exc

    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        return []
    return _parse_articles(payload, images_only=images_only)


async def gdelt_available() -> bool:
    """Report whether GDELT news search can be served — always ``True``.

    GDELT is keyless and needs no configuration, so from the service's standpoint
    it is effectively always available: there is nothing to check. This
    deliberately makes NO network call. ``GetSearchProviders`` invokes it on every
    Search-page mount, and a live reachability GET on that hot path would spend one
    of GDELT's scarce ~1 request / 5s per-IP budget on a result the frontend
    discards — and can 429 the user's own next real search (#1138 review). No
    ProviderKeyReader is ever consulted (keyless).
    """
    return True


async def _fetch_coverage(timespan: str) -> int:
    """One live DOC 2.0 coverage GET → article count for ``timespan``.

    A broad standing query over ``timespan``, counting the returned
    ``articles[]``. A non-dict body or a missing/non-list ``articles`` yields
    ``0``. Any transport/HTTP/JSON failure propagates to the caller
    (:func:`news_coverage`), which decides whether to serve a stale value.
    """
    async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=httpx.Timeout(_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_S)) as client:
        resp = await client.get(
            _DOC_URL,
            params={
                "query": _COVERAGE_QUERY,
                "mode": "ArtList",
                "format": "json",
                "maxrecords": str(_MAX_MAXRECORDS),
                "timespan": timespan,
            },
        )
        resp.raise_for_status()
        payload = resp.json()

    if not isinstance(payload, dict):
        return 0
    articles = payload.get("articles")
    return len(articles) if isinstance(articles, list) else 0


async def news_coverage(timespan: str = "") -> int:
    """Standing recent-article count for the Home CoverageStrip GDELT chip.

    Stub → the fixed :data:`_STUB_COVERAGE_COUNT` (42) immediately, no network
    and no caching (keeps Cypress/CI deterministic). Live → a SERVER-SIDE
    TTL-cached count for ``timespan`` (blank → :data:`_DEFAULT_TIMESPAN`),
    refreshed at most once per :data:`_COVERAGE_TTL_S`. The chip fires on every
    dashboard load, but GDELT allows only ~1 request / 5s per IP, so a live call
    per load gets 429'd (blank chip) and starves real user searches; the cache
    serves a slightly-aged real number instead.

    Concurrency & failure: a :class:`asyncio.Lock` prevents a stampede — one
    coroutine refreshes while others re-check the cache under the lock and reuse
    the fresh value. A failed refresh never propagates: it serves the previous
    cached value (or ``0`` if none) and applies a short
    :data:`_COVERAGE_ERROR_BACKOFF_S` window so an outage doesn't refetch on
    every load. Keyless and DB-free like the search path.
    """
    if _stub_enabled():
        return _STUB_COVERAGE_COUNT

    ts = timespan.strip() or _DEFAULT_TIMESPAN

    cached = _coverage_cache.get(ts)

        _log.info("image proxy total deadline exceeded", host=host)

    except EgressDeniedError as exc:

        raise InvalidImageURL(str(exc)) from exc
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        _log.info("image proxy upstream error", host=host, status=exc.response.status_code)
        raise ImageProxyUnavailable(f"upstream returned {exc.response.status_code}") from exc

async def _read_image(resp: httpx.Response) -> ProxiedImage:
    """Validate the response is an image within the size cap, then read it.

    async for chunk in resp.aiter_bytes():
        buf.extend(chunk)
        if len(buf) > _MAX_BYTES:
            raise ImageProxyRejected("image size exceeds the maximum allowed")

    return ProxiedImage(data=bytes(buf), content_type=content_type)

async def search_web(
    query: str,
    count: int,
    *,
    country_code: str = "",
    time_range: int = search_pb2.SEARCH_TIME_RANGE_UNSPECIFIED,
    safe_search: int = search_pb2.SAFE_SEARCH_UNSPECIFIED,
    domain: str = "",
    result_type: int = search_pb2.WEB_RESULT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED,
    key_reader: ProviderKeyReader,
) -> list[WebResultData]:
    """Run a web search for ``query`` returning up to ``count`` results.

    Mode precedence (see module docstring): stub → canned (reader untouched);
    ``key_reader.get("serper")`` returns a key → live Serper POST; reader
    returns ``None`` → :class:`SearchUnavailable`. A non-positive ``count``
    falls back to :data:`_DEFAULT_COUNT`; a ``count`` above :data:`_MAX_COUNT`
    is clamped down to it.

    Filters (#1135) map onto the Serper request:

    - ``country_code`` (ISO-3166 alpha-2) → ``gl`` (lower-cased); empty means
      worldwide and omits ``gl`` entirely.
    - ``time_range`` (SearchTimeRange enum) → ``tbs=qdr:d|w|m|y`` for
      DAY/WEEK/MONTH/YEAR; ANY/UNSPECIFIED omit ``tbs``.
    - ``safe_search`` (SafeSearch enum) → ``safe=active`` for ON, ``safe=off``
      for OFF; UNSPECIFIED omits ``safe`` entirely (2.0 parity — no forced
      SafeSearch).
    - ``hl`` is always ``en`` (:data:`_HL`) — the interface language 2.0 uses;
      the query is sent as typed and results are translated back downstream.
    - ``domain`` → appended to the query as ``site:<domain>``.
    - ``result_type`` (WebResultType enum) selects the endpoint + response
      array: GENERAL/UNSPECIFIED → ``/search``, IMAGES → ``/images``,
      ACADEMIC → ``/scholar``.
    """
    if _stub_enabled():
        # IMAGES-type stub returns canned image rows (thumbnail + dimensions);
        # VIDEOS-type returns canned video rows (thumbnail + duration/channel/
        # published); every other type returns the organic canned rows.
        if result_type == search_pb2.WEB_RESULT_TYPE_IMAGES:
            return list(_STUB_IMAGE_RESULTS)
        if result_type == search_pb2.WEB_RESULT_TYPE_VIDEOS:
            return list(_STUB_VIDEO_RESULTS)
        return list(_STUB_RESULTS)

    # Broad by design: the ProviderKeyReader Protocol may raise on a store/Vault
    # failure; the adapter translates ANY such failure into its own typed
    # SearchUnavailable rather than coupling to hvac internals or leaking a raw
    # error as gRPC UNKNOWN. (ruff's blind-except rule BLE001 is not enabled in
    # this project, so no noqa is needed.)
    try:
        api_key = await key_reader.get("serper")
    except Exception as exc:
        raise SearchUnavailable("provider key store unavailable") from exc
    if api_key is None:
        raise SearchUnavailable("no web-search provider configured")

    num = min(count, _MAX_COUNT) if count > 0 else _DEFAULT_COUNT

    # ``site:`` is a query-string operator, not a Serper param — fold it into q.
    q = f"{query} site:{domain.strip()}" if domain.strip() else query
    body: dict[str, object] = {"q": q, "num": num, "hl": _HL}
    if country_code.strip():
        body["gl"] = country_code.strip().lower()
    tbs = _TBS_BY_TIME_RANGE.get(time_range)
    if tbs is not None:
        body["tbs"] = tbs
    # 2.0 parity: only an EXPLICIT SafeSearch choice sets ``safe`` — ON →
    # active, OFF → off. UNSPECIFIED omits the param entirely (no forced
    # SafeSearch), matching Serper's own default.
    if safe_search == search_pb2.SAFE_SEARCH_ON:
        body["safe"] = "active"
    elif safe_search == search_pb2.SAFE_SEARCH_OFF:
        body["safe"] = "off"

    url, parser = _ENDPOINTS.get(result_type, (_SEARCH_URL, _parse_organic))

    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=httpx.Timeout(_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_S)) as client:
            resp = await client.post(
                url,
                headers={"X-API-KEY": api_key, "Content-Type": "application/json"},
                json=body,
            )
            resp.raise_for_status()
            # Decode inside the try: a 2xx with a non-JSON body (e.g. a proxy
            # HTML error page during an incident) raises a ValueError
            # (json.JSONDecodeError) here, which must surface as the adapter's
            # own typed SearchUnavailable rather than escaping as gRPC UNKNOWN.
            payload = resp.json()
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        if exc.response.status_code == 429:
            raise SearchThrottled("serper rate limit exceeded") from exc
        raise SearchUnavailable(f"serper returned {exc.response.status_code}") from exc
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise SearchUnavailable(f"serper request failed: {exc}") from exc
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise SearchUnavailable("serper returned a non-JSON response") from exc

    return parser(payload)

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class WebResultData:
    """One organic web-search result, provider-agnostic.

    ``source_domain`` is the host component of ``url`` (``urlparse(...).netloc``)
    with any leading ``www.`` stripped, so badges read ``example.com`` rather
    than ``www.example.com``. Other subdomains (e.g. ``news.example.com``) are
    left intact.

    ``thumbnail_url`` is populated only for IMAGES-type results (the full Serper
    ``imageUrl``, falling back to the small ``thumbnailUrl`` only when no full
    image URL is supplied); every other result class leaves it empty. It is the
    URL the server-side image proxy fetches so the client never contacts the
    image host directly.

    ``image_width`` / ``image_height`` carry the IMAGES-type result's pixel
    dimensions when Serper supplies them (``imageWidth`` / ``imageHeight``); both
    default to 0 — OPTIONAL, so the panel's "Dimensions" spec renders only when
    both are non-zero. Non-image results leave them at 0.

    ``duration`` / ``channel`` / ``published`` carry a VIDEOS-type result's
    provider-formatted runtime (``duration`` e.g. "7:42"), uploader/``channel``
    (e.g. "Vox"), and publish date (``date`` e.g. "Mar 14, 2026"); all three
    default to "" (OPTIONAL, absent) for every other result class (#3034).
    """

    title: str
    url: str
    snippet: str
    source_domain: str
    thumbnail_url: str = ""
    image_width: int = 0
    image_height: int = 0
    duration: str = ""
    channel: str = ""
    published: str = ""


def _as_int(value: object) -> int:
    """Coerce a provider value to a non-negative int, defaulting to 0.

    Serper sends ``imageWidth`` / ``imageHeight`` as JSON numbers, but a missing
    key (``None``), a non-numeric string, or a negative value must all degrade to
    0 — the OPTIONAL "absent" sentinel — rather than raising or emitting garbage.
    """
    try:
        n = int(value)  # type: ignore[call-overload]
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return 0
    return n if n > 0 else 0


def _source_domain(link: str) -> str:
    """Derive a display domain from ``link``: the URL host, minus a leading
    ``www.``. Other subdomains (``news.example.com``) are preserved."""
    host = urlparse(link).netloc
    prefix = "www."
    if host.startswith(prefix):
        return host[len(prefix) :]
    return host


# A YouTube video id is always exactly 11 URL-safe base64 chars. Anchored so a
# longer/shorter capture (a padded or truncated id, a playlist slug) is rejected
# rather than silently pointing the image proxy at a non-existent thumbnail.
_YT_ID_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{11}$")
# Hosts (leading ``www.`` already stripped) whose links carry a YouTube video id.
_YT_HOSTS = frozenset({"youtube.com", "m.youtube.com", "music.youtube.com"})
# ``/<prefix>/<id>`` path shapes that place the id as the second path segment.
_YT_PATH_PREFIXES = frozenset({"shorts", "embed", "v"})


def _youtube_thumbnail(link: str) -> str | None:
    """Derive YouTube's own hi-res thumbnail URL from a video ``link``.

    Serper's ``/videos`` endpoint returns a tiny ``encrypted-tbn0.gstatic.com``
    preview per video, which renders blurry in the detail panel. When the video's
    ``link`` is a YouTube URL, the 11-char video id lets us point the image proxy
    at YouTube's own sharp thumbnail instead (#3034).

    Returns ``https://i.ytimg.com/vi/<id>/hqdefault.jpg`` — the 480x360 variant,
    which ALWAYS exists. ``maxresdefault.jpg`` is deliberately NOT used: it 404s
    for many videos and would break the proxy fetch.

    Handles the common YouTube URL shapes: ``youtube.com/watch?v=<id>``,
    ``youtu.be/<id>``, ``youtube.com/shorts/<id>``, ``youtube.com/embed/<id>``,
    ``youtube.com/v/<id>`` and their ``www.`` / ``m.`` / ``music.`` host
    variants. Returns ``None`` for a non-YouTube link, a missing/invalid (not
    11-char) id, or a malformed URL — it is defensive and never raises, so the
    caller can safely fall back to the Serper-supplied thumbnail.
    """
    try:
        parsed = urlparse(link)
    # urlparse can raise ValueError on a genuinely malformed URL (e.g. a bad
    # IPv6 host or non-numeric port); degrade to "not a YouTube link".
    except ValueError:
        return None
    host = parsed.netloc.lower()
    if host.startswith("www."):
        host = host[len("www.") :]

    video_id: str | None = None
    if host == "youtu.be":
        # youtu.be/<id> — the id is the first path segment.
        video_id = parsed.path.lstrip("/").split("/", 1)[0]
    elif host in _YT_HOSTS:
        if parsed.path == "/watch":
            values = parse_qs(parsed.query).get("v")
            video_id = values[0] if values else None
        else:
            segments = [seg for seg in parsed.path.split("/") if seg]
            if len(segments) >= 2 and segments[0] in _YT_PATH_PREFIXES:
                video_id = segments[1]
    else:
        return None

    if video_id and _YT_ID_RE.match(video_id):
        return f"https://i.ytimg.com/vi/{video_id}/hqdefault.jpg"
    return None


def _stub_enabled() -> bool:
    """True when ``MONITOR_SEARCH_STUB`` is exactly ``"1"``."""

async def serper_available(key_reader: ProviderKeyReader) -> bool:
    """Report whether a web search can be served: stub is on OR a key is stored.

    In stub mode this short-circuits to ``True`` without consulting the reader.
    A capability probe must never hard-fail on a transient store/Vault blip, so
    any reader error degrades to ``False`` ("unavailable") rather than throwing.
    """
    if _stub_enabled():
        return True
    try:
        return (await key_reader.get("serper")) is not None
    # Broad by design: a capability probe degrades to "unavailable" on ANY
    # store/Vault error rather than throwing. (ruff's blind-except rule BLE001
    # is not enabled in this project, so no noqa is needed.)
    except Exception:
        return False

def _parse_organic(payload: dict[str, object]) -> list[WebResultData]:
    """Map a Serper response's ``organic[]`` array into WebResultData.

    Missing ``organic`` (or a non-list value) yields an empty list; each entry's
    ``source_domain`` is derived from its ``link`` host (leading ``www.``
    stripped).
    """
    organic = payload.get("organic")
    if not isinstance(organic, list):
        return []
    results: list[WebResultData] = []
    for item in organic:
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            continue
        link = str(item.get("link", ""))
        results.append(
            WebResultData(
                title=str(item.get("title", "")),
                url=link,
                snippet=str(item.get("snippet", "")),
                source_domain=_source_domain(link),
            )
        )
    return results


def _parse_images(payload: dict[str, object]) -> list[WebResultData]:
    """Map a Serper ``/images`` response's ``images[]`` array (best-effort).

    ``url`` prefers the source page ``link`` (what "View original" should open),
    falling back to the direct ``imageUrl``; ``snippet`` best-efforts to the
    image's ``source`` label. ``source_domain`` is derived from ``url``.

    ``thumbnail_url`` PREFERS the full-resolution ``imageUrl`` (#1135) so the
    card's enlarged tile downscales sharply rather than upscaling the small
    Google preview into a blur; it falls back to the provider ``thumbnailUrl``
    only when no full image URL is supplied. The card renders it via the
    size-capped (5 MiB) server-side image proxy and degrades to the text card on
    error, so a rare oversized image is a harmless fallback.
    """
    images = payload.get("images")
    if not isinstance(images, list):
        return []
    results: list[WebResultData] = []
    for item in images:
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            continue
        image_url = str(item.get("imageUrl", ""))
        link = str(item.get("link", "") or image_url)
        # Prefer the full-resolution imageUrl so the enlarged tile stays crisp;
        # fall back to the small provider thumbnailUrl only when no full image
        # URL is supplied.
        thumbnail = str(image_url or item.get("thumbnailUrl", ""))
        results.append(
            WebResultData(
                title=str(item.get("title", "")),
                url=link,
                snippet=str(item.get("source", "")),
                source_domain=_source_domain(link),
                thumbnail_url=thumbnail,
                # Serper's /images entries carry pixel dimensions; both default to
                # 0 (OPTIONAL "absent") when the provider omits them.
                image_width=_as_int(item.get("imageWidth")),
                image_height=_as_int(item.get("imageHeight")),
            )
        )
    return results


def _parse_videos(payload: dict[str, object]) -> list[WebResultData]:
    """Map a Serper ``/videos`` response's ``videos[]`` array (best-effort, #3034).

    Videos are LINK-OUT only: ``url`` is the source-page ``link`` (what the card
    opens), falling back to the direct ``imageUrl`` if a link is somehow absent;
    ``snippet`` is the item's own ``snippet`` excerpt. ``source_domain`` is
    derived from ``url``.

    ``thumbnail_url`` prefers YouTube's OWN hi-res thumbnail, derived from the
    video id in ``link`` (``i.ytimg.com/vi/<id>/hqdefault.jpg``) — Serper's
    ``/videos`` ``imageUrl`` is a tiny ``encrypted-tbn0.gstatic.com`` preview
    that renders blurry in the detail panel. For a non-YouTube link (vimeo,
    facebook, ...) the derivation returns ``None`` and the thumbnail falls back
    to the full ``imageUrl`` (then the provider ``thumbnailUrl``) exactly as
    before. It is rendered via the size-capped server-side image proxy.
    ``duration`` / ``published`` are provider-formatted strings passed through
    verbatim; ``channel`` prefers the item's ``channel`` and falls back to its
    ``source`` label. Every field defaults to "" when the provider omits it, so a
    minimal item never raises.
    """
    videos = payload.get("videos")
    if not isinstance(videos, list):
        return []
    results: list[WebResultData] = []
    for item in videos:
        if not isinstance(item, dict):
            continue
        image_url = str(item.get("imageUrl", ""))
        link = str(item.get("link", "") or image_url)
        # Prefer YouTube's own sharp thumbnail (derived from the video id); fall
        # back to Serper's full imageUrl, then its small thumbnailUrl.
        thumbnail = _youtube_thumbnail(link) or str(image_url or item.get("thumbnailUrl", ""))
        # Prefer the explicit channel; fall back to the generic source label.
        channel = str(item.get("channel", "") or item.get("source", ""))
        results.append(
            WebResultData(
                title=str(item.get("title", "")),
                url=link,
                snippet=str(item.get("snippet", "")),
                source_domain=_source_domain(link),
                thumbnail_url=thumbnail,
                duration=str(item.get("duration", "")),
                channel=channel,
                published=str(item.get("date", "")),
            )
        )
    return results


# result_type enum -> (endpoint URL, response parser). ACADEMIC uses /scholar,
# whose response reuses the ``organic[]`` shape. UNSPECIFIED behaves as GENERAL.
# VIDEOS uses /videos, whose ``videos[]`` array carries the link-out video rows.

    search_pb2.WEB_RESULT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED: (_SEARCH_URL, _parse_organic),
    search_pb2.WEB_RESULT_TYPE_GENERAL: (_SEARCH_URL, _parse_organic),
    search_pb2.WEB_RESULT_TYPE_IMAGES: (_IMAGES_URL, _parse_images),
    search_pb2.WEB_RESULT_TYPE_ACADEMIC: (_SCHOLAR_URL, _parse_organic),
    search_pb2.WEB_RESULT_TYPE_VIDEOS: (_VIDEOS_URL, _parse_videos),
}


async def search_web(
    query: str,
    count: int,
    *,
    country_code: str = "",
    time_range: int = search_pb2.SEARCH_TIME_RANGE_UNSPECIFIED,
    safe_search: int = search_pb2.SAFE_SEARCH_UNSPECIFIED,
    domain: str = "",
    result_type: int = search_pb2.WEB_RESULT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED,
    key_reader: ProviderKeyReader,
) -> list[WebResultData]:
    """Run a web search for ``query`` returning up to ``count`` results.

    Mode precedence (see module docstring): stub → canned (reader untouched);
    ``key_reader.get("serper")`` returns a key → live Serper POST; reader
    returns ``None`` → :class:`SearchUnavailable`. A non-positive ``count``
    falls back to :data:`_DEFAULT_COUNT`; a ``count`` above :data:`_MAX_COUNT`
    is clamped down to it.

    Filters (#1135) map onto the Serper request:

    - ``country_code`` (ISO-3166 alpha-2) → ``gl`` (lower-cased); empty means
      worldwide and omits ``gl`` entirely.
    - ``time_range`` (SearchTimeRange enum) → ``tbs=qdr:d|w|m|y`` for
      DAY/WEEK/MONTH/YEAR; ANY/UNSPECIFIED omit ``tbs``.
    - ``safe_search`` (SafeSearch enum) → ``safe=active`` for ON, ``safe=off``
      for OFF; UNSPECIFIED omits ``safe`` entirely (2.0 parity — no forced
      SafeSearch).
    - ``hl`` is always ``en`` (:data:`_HL`) — the interface language 2.0 uses;
      the query is sent as typed and results are translated back downstream.
    - ``domain`` → appended to the query as ``site:<domain>``.
    - ``result_type`` (WebResultType enum) selects the endpoint + response
      array: GENERAL/UNSPECIFIED → ``/search``, IMAGES → ``/images``,
      ACADEMIC → ``/scholar``.
    """
    if _stub_enabled():
        # IMAGES-type stub returns canned image rows (thumbnail + dimensions);
        # VIDEOS-type returns canned video rows (thumbnail + duration/channel/
        # published); every other type returns the organic canned rows.
        if result_type == search_pb2.WEB_RESULT_TYPE_IMAGES:
            return list(_STUB_IMAGE_RESULTS)
        if result_type == search_pb2.WEB_RESULT_TYPE_VIDEOS:
            return list(_STUB_VIDEO_RESULTS)
        return list(_STUB_RESULTS)

    # Broad by design: the ProviderKeyReader Protocol may raise on a store/Vault
    # failure; the adapter translates ANY such failure into its own typed
    # SearchUnavailable rather than coupling to hvac internals or leaking a raw
    # error as gRPC UNKNOWN. (ruff's blind-except rule BLE001 is not enabled in
    # this project, so no noqa is needed.)
    try:
        api_key = await key_reader.get("serper")
    except Exception as exc:
        raise SearchUnavailable("provider key store unavailable") from exc
    if api_key is None:
        raise SearchUnavailable("no web-search provider configured")

    num = min(count, _MAX_COUNT) if count > 0 else _DEFAULT_COUNT

    # ``site:`` is a query-string operator, not a Serper param — fold it into q.
    q = f"{query} site:{domain.strip()}" if domain.strip() else query
    body: dict[str, object] = {"q": q, "num": num, "hl": _HL}
    if country_code.strip():
        body["gl"] = country_code.strip().lower()
    tbs = _TBS_BY_TIME_RANGE.get(time_range)
    if tbs is not None:
        body["tbs"] = tbs
    # 2.0 parity: only an EXPLICIT SafeSearch choice sets ``safe`` — ON →
    # active, OFF → off. UNSPECIFIED omits the param entirely (no forced
    # SafeSearch), matching Serper's own default.
    if safe_search == search_pb2.SAFE_SEARCH_ON:
        body["safe"] = "active"
    elif safe_search == search_pb2.SAFE_SEARCH_OFF:
        body["safe"] = "off"

    url, parser = _ENDPOINTS.get(result_type, (_SEARCH_URL, _parse_organic))

    try:
        async with httpx.AsyncClient(timeout=httpx.Timeout(_SEARCH_TIMEOUT_S)) as client:
            resp = await client.post(
                url,
                headers={"X-API-KEY": api_key, "Content-Type": "application/json"},
                json=body,
            )
            resp.raise_for_status()
            # Decode inside the try: a 2xx with a non-JSON body (e.g. a proxy
            # HTML error page during an incident) raises a ValueError
            # (json.JSONDecodeError) here, which must surface as the adapter's
            # own typed SearchUnavailable rather than escaping as gRPC UNKNOWN.
            payload = resp.json()
    except httpx.HTTPStatusError as exc:
        if exc.response.status_code == 429:
            raise SearchThrottled("serper rate limit exceeded") from exc
        raise SearchUnavailable(f"serper returned {exc.response.status_code}") from exc
    except httpx.HTTPError as exc:
        raise SearchUnavailable(f"serper request failed: {exc}") from exc
    except ValueError as exc:
        raise SearchUnavailable("serper returned a non-JSON response") from exc

    return parser(payload)

If you want to:

- **Regenerate proto stubs (Go/Python/TS)**: `make proto`
- **Regenerate only TS proto stubs**: `make proto-ts`
- **Lint proto**: `make proto-lint`
- **Check proto breaking changes**: `make proto-breaking`
- **Run Go tests for a service**: `cd services/<svc> && go test -short ./...` (or `make <svc>-test`)
- **Run one Go test by name**: `go test -run '^TestName$' ./internal/...`
- **Run Go integration tests**: `go test -tags=integration -run '^TestName$' ./tests/integration/...` (or `make <svc>-test-int`, Docker required)
- **Run all Go modules + coverage file**: `make go-test` (or `make go-test-short` to skip testcontainers)
- **Check Go coverage gate**: `make go-coverage`
- **Tidy Go modules**: `make go-tidy`
- **Vet Go code**: `go vet ./...` (from service dir)
- **Run Vitest for one workspace**: `pnpm test`
- **Watch Vitest (TDD loop)**: `pnpm test:watch`
- **Run one Vitest test by name**: `pnpm test -- --run -t "<name>"`
- **Run Vitest with coverage**: `pnpm test -- --coverage`
- **Recompile Paraglide i18n messages**: `pnpm --filter @omnicore-platform/platform-chrome run compile-messages` (then hand-wire `frontends/platform-chrome/src/paraglide/messages.ts`)
- **Audit i18n locale parity/ICU/glossary**: `npx tsx scripts/i18n-audit.ts`
- **Fast glossary-only i18n check**: `cd frontends/platform-chrome && ./node_modules/.bin/vitest run tests/glossary.regression.test.ts`
- **Regenerate Range location-wizard geo shards (offline)**: `npx tsx scripts/geo-generate.ts` (network refresh: `npx tsx scripts/geo-generate.ts --fetch` first, to repopulate `scripts/geo-sources/`)
- **Lint an MFE**: `pnpm lint`
- **Typecheck an MFE**: `pnpm typecheck`
- **Bring up the whole stack (baked images)**: `make up` (`SCOPE=<vertical>` to limit, `CLEAN=1` to wipe volumes, `BUILD=1` to rebuild images from fresh proto)
- **`make up` never builds two MFE images at once — not even the ones `BUILD=` did not name**: each Vite build takes an 8GB Node heap, so the guarded loop (`_build-guarded`) builds non-MFE images in parallel and MFE images strictly one at a time. That guard used to cover only the `BUILD=`-selected set, while `up`'s final `docker compose up -d` carried no `--no-build` and every locally-built service keeps its `build:` context — so anything `BUILD=` missed and `stack-pin-images.py` could not snapshot (which is *everything* on a machine with no bare `:dev` tags left to snapshot from) was built by **compose** instead, all at once. 11 concurrent Vite builds either die with `ResourceExhausted: process "/bin/sh -c pnpm run build" ... cannot allocate memory` or drives an OOM-kill spiral that wedges the Docker daemon, so `make up` just *hangs* with no error at all. `up` now plans the absent set itself (`platform/scripts/plan-implicit-builds.py`), builds it through the same guard, and passes `--no-build` so any remaining hole fails loudly instead of fanning out. `make dev` deliberately keeps compose's implicit build: its MFE layer is host-side vite servers, not containers, so only service images can be built there. Tests: `python3 -m pytest platform/scripts/test_build_guarded.py platform/scripts/test_plan_implicit_builds.py -q`.
- **AI backend mode (unified across verticals, `omnicore_svc_runtime.ai`)**: real inference-server litellm/vLLM (over Tailscale) is now the default for `make up`/`make dev` — `AI_DEV_MODE` is unset/false in `.env.example`. `AI_TEST_MODE=true` → StubLLM (deterministic, wins over `AI_DEV_MODE`). `AI_DEV_MODE=true` → local Ollama backend (`platform/compose/ollama.yml`, litellm alias `ollama-dev`). Old per-service flags (`STUDIO_AI_DEV_MODE`, `RANGE_AI_DEV_MODE`, `DIALOGUE_AI_DRAFT_DEV_MODE`) are gone — hard cutover. Per-vertical model pins (`RANGE_LITELLM_GEN_MODEL`, default `qwen3.5:9b`; `STUDIO_LITELLM_GEN_MODEL`, default `gpt-oss:20b`; `LITELLM_DRAFT_MODEL` for dialogue, default `gpt-oss:20b`) live as env-overridable defaults in `range-svc.yml`/`range-svc-worker.yml`/`studio-svc.yml`/`studio-svc-worker.yml`/`dialogue-svc.yml`/`dialogue-svc-worker.yml`.
- **Boot-time AI reachability probe + offline/force-live escape hatches**: `make up`/`make dev` run a preflight (`platform/scripts/ai-live-probe.py`) before compose starts, checking each in-scope AI-capable vertical's resolved model against the real gateway. Reachable → live mode, printed per-vertical. Unreachable with local Ollama available → loud degraded-fallback banner, never a silent per-call swap. Unreachable with no Ollama → the target fails outright. `OFFLINE=1` (formerly `RANGE_AI_MODE`, now `AI_OFFLINE_MODE`, vertical-scope-agnostic) skips the probe entirely and forces local Ollama — airplane-mode / no-Tailscale case. `REQUIRE_LIVE=1` turns an unreachable gateway into a hard failure instead of a degraded fallback. `STUB=1` means `AI_TEST_MODE=true` (deterministic StubLLM) — it does NOT mean local Ollama; use `OFFLINE=1` for that.
- **Hot-reload dev stack (services + MFEs)**: `make dev` (`SCOPE=` honored)
- **Boot an isolated walled local stack (own compose project, own hostname, one published port)**: `make up STACK=<name>` — needs `*.localhost` to resolve, which works out of the box on macOS (no other OS supported yet). Not seeded automatically: a fresh stack has no users until you also run `make seed STACK=<name>`.
- **Hot-reload a walled local stack**: `make dev STACK=<name>` — the walled overlay is derived from `dev`'s OWN compose file set (never `up`'s), so a scoped `dev` never references a service (e.g. an MFE container) that `dev` itself doesn't bring up, and shell-bff's dev-mode volumes (the `/workspace` bind + Go module/build caches) survive the per-stack mtls rewrite instead of being silently dropped.
- **A bare `make up` in a worktree warns before driving the SHARED stack**: `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME ?= omnicore-platform` is identical in every worktree and is only reassigned inside the `STACK=` block, so `make up` / `dev` / `seed` / `down` / `clean` / `cypress-run` with no `STACK=` drives that ONE project and its volumes from whatever worktree you happen to be in. `up`/`dev`/`seed`/`down`/`clean`/`cypress-*` now print the derived `STACK=<name>` you probably wanted and pause 3s. It is warn-only, never fatal — silence it with `OMNICORE_NO_STACK_WARN=1` (or pass `STACK=platform` to say you meant the shared one). Silent in the primary checkout, which legitimately owns that project.
- **List running local stacks and their URLs**: `make stacks` — the state column is `up` / `down` / `orphaned` / `orphaned-up`. `orphaned` means the worktree that owned the pin no longer exists on disk; `orphaned-up` means that AND it is still live and serving, so its port must not be reused.
- **Drop pins whose worktree is gone**: `make stack-gc` (`DRY=1` to preview). Nothing used to remove a pin except an explicit `release` run from the owning worktree, so a `git worktree remove` left its entry behind forever, holding a name and a port. `gc` deliberately refuses to drop an `orphaned-up` pin — that stack is still serving, and freeing its port would let a second stack claim it.
- **Retire a stack for good**: `make stack-release STACK=<name>` — drops the registry pin, this worktree's generated `.omnicore/` files for it, AND its per-stack image tags. Prefer this over `stack.py release` now that image tags are per-stack, since the bare script cannot clean those up (it owns identity only, no docker).
- **Print one stack's URL**: `make stack-url STACK=<name>`
- **Seed a walled stack's default data**: `make seed STACK=<name>` (same idempotent seed as the primary — 1 org + 1 workspace + 10 role-combo users + 1 range exercise; `make seed` with no `STACK=` seeds the primary)
- **Open psql against a walled stack's postgres**: `make psql STACK=<name>`
- **Publish a walled stack's postgres+nats on two extra host ports for GUI DB clients**: `DB_PORTS=1` (only meaningful with `STACK=<name>`, e.g. `make up STACK=review DB_PORTS=1`)
- **Hot-reload one MFE into a walled stack**: `make <vertical>-mfe-dev-federated STACK=<name>` — routes `/<vertical>-mfe/` through that stack's own ingress to your local vite server instead of the baked image. Safe to run for several MFEs at once in the same stack: each invocation re-reads every OTHER live `--hot` MFE's probed port from `.omnicore/hot-<stack>-*.port` and re-adds it, so starting a second one doesn't 502 the first; the port file is removed automatically when that MFE's dev server exits.
- **Run the cross-stack isolation gate (12 vectors)**: `make stack-isolation-test STACK_A=<name> STACK_B=<name>` (both stacks already up; the unwalled primary's name here is `platform`, e.g. `STACK_A=platform`)
- **Reach a walled stack's admin consoles**: same single published port, different sub-hostnames — `auth.<name>.localhost:<port>` (Keycloak), `grafana.<name>.localhost:<port>`, `minio.<name>.localhost:<port>`, `prom.<name>.localhost:<port>`
- **Reach a walled stack's Vault**: no ingress route and no host port, deliberately — `docker exec` into the stack's vault container (see `make vault-pki-bootstrap`)
- **Provision mTLS PKI for a walled stack**: `make vault-pki-bootstrap STACK=<name>` — writes issued certs to that stack's own `.omnicore/secrets-<name>/mtls` tree (`CA_OUT_DIR`) instead of the shared `platform/secrets/mtls` the unwalled path uses.
- **Force a stack's pinned port to re-probe**: `python3 platform/scripts/stack.py resolve --stack <name> --reprobe` — only needed when something else grabbed the previously-pinned port while the stack was down; a plain `make up STACK=<name>` never re-probes an already-pinned, currently-live port out from under itself.
- **Where stack names/ports are pinned**: `~/.omnicore/stacks.json`, machine-wide (NOT per-worktree) — a stack name becomes a hostname and a compose project, both of which are machine-global, so one registry arbitrates them across every worktree. The generated artifacts (ingress config, walled overlay, per-stack secrets, hot-port files) stay in each worktree's own `.omnicore/`, since they are built from that worktree's source.
- **A stack name belongs to the worktree that created it**: reusing the same `STACK=<name>` from a different worktree is refused, not silently shared — `stack 'x' is owned by a different worktree -- refusing to touch it.` naming both paths. Without this, two worktrees would resolve the same compose project and the second `make up` would recreate the first's containers from its own source, i.e. a reviewer's stack silently serving another branch's code. Pick a different name (`make up STACK=<name>-2`) or release it with `python3 platform/scripts/stack.py release <name>`.
- **Pact broker across stacks**: shared by design, not per-stack — a `STACK=<name>` `pact-publish`/`pact-verify`/`pact-smoke` still targets the ONE broker at `localhost:9292`, same broker CI uses
- **litellm/GPU is NOT shared across walled stacks** (deviation from the design spec's §8, which called for a shared `omnicore-shared` litellm project): each walled stack runs its own ~792 MiB litellm container. The GPU can't be meaningfully partitioned, so a real shared instance is future work; until then, budget ~792 MiB/stack for it specifically, on top of the capacity figures below.
- **Local stack capacity**: one walled stack is ~76 containers behind one published port, ~50-80s to boot. - **See every build/test/stack target**: `make help`

## CI runs on the promotion to `develop`, not on the PR

Everything that costs GitHub Actions minutes now fires on `push` to `develop`,
the promotion of `main`: Go `-race` + coverage gate, frontend unit + coverage,
Python *integration* (testcontainers), migration lint, i18n, pact, proto
compatibility, image build/sign/verify, and all eight Cypress lanes.

**Python lint/typecheck/unit is the exception, as of #2811.** `python-test.yml`
had no `pull_request` trigger at all, so no ruff, `mypy --strict` or pytest run
touched a PR *or* the merge to `main` — a Python regression could not surface
before the promotion. Its cheap legs (`py lint`, `lint + typecheck + unit`,
`lint + typecheck (shared python libs)`) now run on PRs; they were already on
`ubuntu-24-arm-2core` and the `changes` job scopes both matrices to the services
a PR touches. The heavy `integration (<svc>)` matrix stays promotion-only —
that is the half the original cost argument was about.

The cheap class still runs on the PR, again on the merge commit to `main`, and
again on the promotion to `develop`. It runs on `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` — a
GitHub-hosted ARM64 larger runner: billed, but at the ARM rate, out of its own
concurrency pool rather than the plan's 60 standard slots, and seconds-to-a-few-
minutes per job. So `main` keeps per-merge signal for these:

| Check | Workflow | Runner |
|---|---|---|
| Markdown lint, Compose config validation, Keycloak realm-export lint, Branch-protection doc sync, Load-harness lib tests | `ci.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Secret Scan (gitleaks) | `secret-scan.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Action Lint | `security-scans.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Go Vuln Scan (govulncheck) | `security-scans.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| golangci-lint (new-issues-only) | `go-test.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, **PR only** |
| py lint / lint + typecheck + unit (`<svc>`), lint + typecheck (shared python libs) | `python-test.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, PR + develop (scoped to changed services; `integration (<svc>)` stays develop-only) |
| No duplicate Prometheus metrics in a boot graph | `ci.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` |
| Smoke test — cosign rejects unsigned image | `sign-and-verify.yml` | `ubuntu-24-arm-2core`, PR + develop (that workflow has no `main` trigger) |
| go test -short (every changed module) | `go-test.yml` | self-hosted, **push to `main` only** |

### The self-hosted mac fleet no longer runs anything on a PR

That is #2372 [P1-26], not a capacity choice: PR-branch code executing on a
persistent shared host is the finding, and its acceptance criterion is "move
required checks off PR-triggered self-hosted runners". Do not put a
`pull_request` workload back on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — that reopens a
P1. A merge commit on `main` is post-review code, which is the trust boundary
the finding draws, so the fleet can still run push-to-main work.

`go test -short` is the one job that uses that: the half of the Go suite that
needs no Docker (it skips every testcontainers test, the same way
`make go-test-short` does), so the merge to `main` gets free compile + unit
coverage of every changed module. A PR gets `golangci-lint` plus whatever
`make pr-preflight` you ran locally. The `-race` + testcontainers matrix and
the coverage gate wait for develop, and `go-test-short` does not run there
because `test-module` supersedes it.

`golangci-lint` is PR-only for a different reason: its `--new-from-rev`
new-issues-only gate is what makes linting a never-before-linted ~32-module
repo tractable, and there is no merge-base equivalent on a push. `test-module`
and the coverage gate treat a skipped `go-lint` as pass-through.

Anything running Go on the fleet MUST provision through
`.github/actions/mac-toolchain`. Each host runs twelve runner processes against
one `$HOME`, so a shared GOROOT that any job may `rm -rf` corrupts a sibling's
link step — that is why govulncheck was moved off the fleet once before
("cannot open file DO NOT USE - main build pseudo-cache built"). The action
keys GOROOT by version and installs via atomic `mv`, never mutating a tree in
use.

Cheap hosted jobs ride along because the ones above depend on them: the
`changes` and `prepare-proto` pair in both `go-test.yml` and
`security-scans.yml` (golangci-lint, `go test` and govulncheck all need
generated proto stubs).

Every billed heavy job is pinned to
`github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'` — NOT to
`push` alone, because a merge to `main` is also a push event. `sign-and-verify`
is the one workflow with no `main` trigger at all: it keeps its `pull_request`
trigger only so the cosign smoke check reports there, and every other job in it
is develop-pinned, so a PR schedules exactly that one job.

Consequences worth internalizing:

- **A required check that reports `skipped` counts as PASSED.** `go test +
  coverage gate` is pinned to push:develop, so on a PR it resolves green without
  running anything. Do not read it as signal, and do not re-add it to the `main`
  ruleset. `Smoke test — cosign rejects unsigned image` is the counter-example
  and deliberately so: #2369 un-skipped it precisely because a skipped required
  check proved nothing, so it really does run on every PR.
- **`make pr-preflight` is now the real pre-merge check, not a preview of one.**
  It runs CI's own unit/lint/type/coverage/proto/migration/i18n commands at the
  changed scope. `INT=1` adds the testcontainer integration suites — still worth
  running, since Python integration remains promotion-only. If it isn't green
  locally, nothing downstream will catch it until the promotion. For the
  complete picture — including image builds, pact, and every Cypress spec —
  `make full-local-pass` chains every gate in dependency order.
- **`main` catches the cheap class, `develop` catches the rest.** A lint,
  gitleaks, actionlint, markdown or Python lint/type/unit regression fails on the
  merge commit that introduced it. A Go test, coverage, Python integration, pact,
  image-build or Cypress regression does not surface until the promotion.
- **A duplicate module-level Prometheus metric never starts the service.**
  `prometheus_client`'s registry is process-global, so a second registration of
  the same name raises `ValueError: Duplicated timeseries` at *import*. No unit
  test covers it (each service imports only its own module) and no path filter
  catches it (#2811's arming commit touched none of the seven services it broke).
  `platform/scripts/metric-registry-collisions.py` walks every service's boot
  import graph on each PR. Run it directly with
  `python3 platform/scripts/metric-registry-collisions.py`.
- **A red `develop` names a batch, not a commit.** Everything that merged to
  `main` since the last promotion is in scope. Bisect with
  `git log --oneline <last-good-develop>..develop`, and prefer promoting often
  so that range stays short.

## Testing policy — Cypress e2e

Cypress UI e2e rides in the feature branch. Any PR that adds or changes a user-facing surface owes a spec under `frontends/cypress/cypress/e2e/<vertical>/`, landed in the same branch — as does any change to login, session, invite, or org-role gating, UI diff or not. Backend-only PRs (proto, migration, service handler, BFF route with no UI consumer) don't.

Ownership is split by file, not by team:

- **Feature dev owns:** the spec files themselves, and `support/selectors.ts`.
- **QA/QC-stewarded:** the shared foundation — `cypress.config.ts`, `support/{e2e,commands,personas}.ts`, `tasks/**`, `fixtures/personas.json`.

Two things that bite:

- A spec absent from a workflow's `--spec` list did not run. Wiring it into the relevant GitHub workflow is part of authoring the spec — check that the workflow actually seeds the state the spec needs.
- `e2e.yml` is non-required and posts no check, so a green PR is not evidence a spec ran. Verify locally against `make up`.

# Frontend design system guardrails

- Per `tdd-react` on `tailwind.preset.ts` as the source of truth for `cog-*`: an
  undefined token emits no CSS and is silently invisible, not an error. This branch
  found 52 phantom tokens across 233 occurrences, including 3 passing tests that
  asserted classes rendering nothing. Grep the preset before using any `cog-*` class
  — a test asserting an undefined class is not a safety net.
- **Never inline raw hex or arbitrary Tailwind values** (`text-[#fff]`,
  `border-[1.5px]`) at a call site — define a token in the preset instead.
- **Bare numeric spacing/size utilities are banned** (`p-4`, `gap-6`, `min-h-11`) in
  favor of named `cog-*` rungs. For hit targets specifically, use `min-h-tap` /
  `min-w-tap` (44px) — never `min-h-11`.
- **WCAG 2.5.8 hit areas:** don't enlarge the visible box to hit 44×44. Move the
  drawn box into an inner `aria-hidden` span at its original size, and put the tap
  rungs on the interactive element wrapping it. Applied 7x this branch — follow the
  established pattern rather than inventing a new one.
- **Any new axis added to `tailwind.preset.ts`'s `theme.extend` must be registered in
  `frontends/ui/src/lib/cn.ts`'s `extendTailwindMerge` config.** An unregistered axis
  makes `tailwind-merge` silently DELETE one of two conflicting classes — 5 live
  defects found this branch from exactly this (`text-heading-md`, `bg-cog-ai`,
  `shadow-cog-e1`, `border-field`, letterSpacing). The `CN_axis_parity` rule in
  `platform/scripts/design-ratchet.mjs` gates it.
- **`Design parity` (`platform/scripts/design-ratchet.mjs --ci`) is PR-blocking.**
  Its counts are ratchets — they may only go down, never up. A matcher change
  requires re-running with `--update` in the same PR, so the rule diff and the count
  diff review together.
- Test process for any change here: see the `tdd-react` skill.

Everything that costs GitHub Actions minutes now fires on `push` to `develop`,

compatibility, image build/sign/verify, and all eight Cypress lanes.

**Python lint/typecheck/unit is the exception, as of #2811.** `python-test.yml`
had no `pull_request` trigger at all, so no ruff, `mypy --strict` or pytest run
touched a PR *or* the merge to `main` — a Python regression could not surface
before the promotion. Its cheap legs (`py lint`, `lint + typecheck + unit`,
`lint + typecheck (shared python libs)`) now run on PRs; they were already on

a PR touches. The heavy `integration (<svc>)` matrix stays promotion-only —
that is the half the original cost argument was about.

again on the promotion to `develop`. It runs on `ubuntu-24-arm-2core` — a

### The self-hosted mac fleet no longer runs anything on a PR

That is #2372 [P1-26], not a capacity choice: PR-branch code executing on a
persistent shared host is the finding, and its acceptance criterion is "move
required checks off PR-triggered self-hosted runners". Do not put a
`pull_request` workload back on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]` — that reopens a
P1. A merge commit on `main` is post-review code, which is the trust boundary
the finding draws, so the fleet can still run push-to-main work.

`go test -short` is the one job that uses that: the half of the Go suite that
needs no Docker (it skips every testcontainers test, the same way
`make go-test-short` does), so the merge to `main` gets free compile + unit
coverage of every changed module. A PR gets `golangci-lint` plus whatever
`make pr-preflight` you ran locally. The `-race` + testcontainers matrix and
the coverage gate wait for develop, and `go-test-short` does not run there
because `test-module` supersedes it.

`golangci-lint` is PR-only for a different reason: its `--new-from-rev`
new-issues-only gate is what makes linting a never-before-linted ~32-module
repo tractable, and there is no merge-base equivalent on a push. `test-module`
and the coverage gate treat a skipped `go-lint` as pass-through.

Anything running Go on the fleet MUST provision through
`.github/actions/mac-toolchain`. Each host runs twelve runner processes against
one `$HOME`, so a shared GOROOT that any job may `rm -rf` corrupts a sibling's
link step — that is why govulncheck was moved off the fleet once before
("cannot open file DO NOT USE - main build pseudo-cache built"). The action
keys GOROOT by version and installs via atomic `mv`, never mutating a tree in
use.

Cheap hosted jobs ride along because the ones above depend on them: the
`changes` and `prepare-proto` pair in both `go-test.yml` and
`security-scans.yml` (golangci-lint, `go test` and govulncheck all need
generated proto stubs).

Every billed heavy job is pinned to
`github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/develop'` — NOT to
`push` alone, because a merge to `main` is also a push event. `sign-and-verify`
is the one workflow with no `main` trigger at all: it keeps its `pull_request`
trigger only so the cosign smoke check reports there, and every other job in it
is develop-pinned, so a PR schedules exactly that one job.

- **A required check that reports `skipped` counts as PASSED.** `go test +
  coverage gate` is pinned to push:develop, so on a PR it resolves green without
  running anything. Do not read it as signal, and do not re-add it to the `main`
  ruleset. `Smoke test — cosign rejects unsigned image` is the counter-example
  and deliberately so: #2369 un-skipped it precisely because a skipped required
  check proved nothing, so it really does run on every PR.
- **`make pr-preflight` is now the real pre-merge check, not a preview of one.**
  It runs CI's own unit/lint/type/coverage/proto/migration/i18n commands at the
  changed scope. `INT=1` adds the testcontainer integration suites — still worth
  running, since Python integration remains promotion-only. If it isn't green
  locally, nothing downstream will catch it until the promotion. For the
  complete picture — including image builds, pact, and every Cypress spec —
  `make full-local-pass` chains every gate in dependency order.
- **`main` catches the cheap class, `develop` catches the rest.** A lint,
  gitleaks, actionlint, markdown or Python lint/type/unit regression fails on the
  merge commit that introduced it. A Go test, coverage, Python integration, pact,
  image-build or Cypress regression does not surface until the promotion.
- **A duplicate module-level Prometheus metric never starts the service.**
  `prometheus_client`'s registry is process-global, so a second registration of
  the same name raises `ValueError: Duplicated timeseries` at *import*. No unit
  test covers it (each service imports only its own module) and no path filter
  catches it (#2811's arming commit touched none of the seven services it broke).
  `platform/scripts/metric-registry-collisions.py` walks every service's boot
  import graph on each PR. Run it directly with
  `python3 platform/scripts/metric-registry-collisions.py`.
- **A red `develop` names a batch, not a commit.** Everything that merged to
  `main` since the last promotion is in scope. Bisect with
  `git log --oneline <last-good-develop>..develop`, and prefer promoting often
  so that range stays short.

Cypress UI e2e rides in the feature branch.
